name: Digital Forensics
description: Skills related to the forensic acquisition, analysis, and reporting of digital evidence. Covers multiple evidence sources (disk, memory, network, mobile, cloud) and malware analysis. Aligned with ILAC-G19 forensic science guidance.

categories.name: Disk Forensics
categories.description: Forensic acquisition and analysis of storage media. Covers disk imaging, filesystem analysis, file recovery, timeline analysis, and artifact extraction from Windows, Linux, and macOS systems.

categories.name: Memory Forensics
categories.description: Acquisition and analysis of volatile memory. Covers memory imaging, process analysis, network connection reconstruction, malware detection in memory, and rootkit identification.

categories.name: Network Forensics
categories.description: Capture and analysis of network traffic for forensic purposes. Covers packet capture, flow analysis, protocol reconstruction, network artifact extraction, and covert channel detection.

categories.name: Mobile Forensics
categories.description: Forensic acquisition and analysis of mobile devices (iOS, Android). Covers logical and physical acquisition, app data extraction, communication analysis, and location data analysis.

categories.name: Cloud Forensics
categories.description: Forensic investigation in cloud environments. Covers log acquisition, API-based evidence collection, cloud-specific artifact analysis, and multi-tenant investigation challenges.

categories.name: Malware Analysis
categories.description: Analysis of malicious software. Covers static analysis, dynamic analysis (sandboxing), behavioral analysis, code-level reverse engineering, and C2 infrastructure analysis.

categories.name: Incident Response
categories.description: Handling and technical response to security incidents. Covers incident coordination and notification, live response and triage collection, scoping, and containment, eradication, and recovery while preserving evidence.
